gloss: not, do not; nothing, of no worth; (oak)
summary: אַל is the negative of wish and command: “do not”, “let not”, and on its own “no!”. Scripture also uses it as a noun, “nothing” (“make my word nothing”, Job 24:25), and the noun אֱלִיל, “nothing, thing of no worth”, is built on the same letters: Job's comforters are “healers of nothing” and the gods of the nations are אֱלִילִים, nothings, while Yahweh made the heavens. So the particle is taken as a word of a root אלל, “be nothing, be of no worth”; but no verb of the root is found in scripture and the link rests on these two words and on Akkadian, which has both ul “not” and ulālu “weak, helpless”, so it is a working reading, not a proven one. The oak, אַלּוֹן and אַלָּה, shares the spelling; how it is tied to the rest is not known.

words.gloss: not, do not, let not; no!; nothing
words.summary: The negative of what is wished or commanded, never of plain fact, which is לֹא: “may he not let your foot slip; may your keeper not slumber” is followed by “he will not (לֹא) slumber” (Psa 121:3–4). It stands before a jussive verb, before a noun (“no death”, “no rest”), alone as an answer (“no!”), and once as a noun, “nothing”. Ugaritic, Phoenician, Sabaic, Ge'ez and Akkadian all have the same negative.

senses.definition: With a second-person verb it forbids or urges against something: do not do it.

evidence.note: Moses to Hobab: אַל־נָא תַּעֲזֹב אֹתָנוּ, “please do not leave us”, for he knows where Israel should camp in the wilderness.
אַל־תִּפְנוּ אֶל־הָאֱלִילִם, “do not turn to the nothings”: the command, beside לֹא with the imperfect in the same verse.
“Do not come near here; put off your sandals.”
“Do not drink wine or strong drink … when you go into the tent of meeting.”
“Only do not rebel against Yahweh, and do not fear the people of the land.”
“Do not harden your heart as at Meribah”, quoted in Heb 3:8, 15 and 4:7 with μή.
μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν, quoting Psa 95:8.

senses.definition: With a first- or third-person verb it wishes or prays that something may not be.

evidence.note: “May he not give your foot to slipping; may your keeper not slumber”, answered in 121:4 by the fact, with לֹא: “he will not slumber nor sleep”.
“In you I trust: let me not be ashamed; let not my enemies exult over me.”
“Let there not be strife between me and you.”
Aaron for Miriam: “let her not be as one dead.”
“Mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew nor rain on you.”

senses.definition: On its own, or before a vocative, it refuses what has been said or proposed: no!

evidence.note: Elisha says “go to the prophets of your father”; the king answers אַל, “No, for Yahweh has called these three kings …”.
אַל בְּנֹתַי, “No, my daughters!”
Lot: אַל־נָא אֲדֹנָי, “Oh no, my lords!”
אַל־בְּנִי, “No, my son.”
אַל־אַחַי, “No, my brothers!”
Tamar refuses Amnon's sending her away.

senses.definition: Before a noun it denies that the thing is there or is fitting: no …, not for ….

evidence.note: “In the path of righteousness is life, and the way of its path is אַל־מָוֶת, no death”: אַל־מָוֶת is set in parallel with חַיִּים.
אַל־דֳּמִי־לָךְ, “let there be no rest to you”, beside “do not be silent, do not be still”.
אַל־דֳּמִי לָכֶם, “no rest to you”, to the watchmen who remind Yahweh.
אַל לַמְּלָכִים, “not for kings to drink wine.”

senses.definition: Once it is itself a noun: what is not, nothing.

evidence.note: “If it is not so, who will prove me a liar, and make my word לְאַל, into nothing?”
μὴ σκληρύνητε, quoting Psa 95:8's אַל־תַּקְשׁוּ.

parallels.note: The negative of fact beside the negative of wish: “may he not slumber … he will not slumber” (Psa 121:3–4); “do not turn … you shall not make” (Lev 19:4).

opposites.note: “Life” in the path of righteousness, and on its way אַל־מָוֶת, “no death”.

evidence.note: “Do not fear, Abram; I am your shield.”
“Do not fear, for I am with you.”
וְאַל־תִּתְּנוּ דֳמִי לוֹ, “and give him no rest.”

phrases.gloss: make into nothing, bring to nothing

words.summary: Scripture's Aramaic uses the same negative of wish and command, in Daniel only. The corpus files every אַל under this Aramaic key as well as the Hebrew one, so its count here is the Hebrew's.

senses.definition: With a jussive verb, it urges or wishes that something may not happen.

evidence.note: Daniel to Arioch: “Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon; bring me in before the king.”
“Let not the dream or its interpretation alarm you.”
The queen: “Let not your thoughts alarm you, and let not your brightness be changed.”

words.gloss: nothing, thing of no worth; (pl.) the nothings, the nations' gods
words.summary: A noun of the same letters as אַל, set beside it in Lev 19:4 (אַל־תִּפְנוּ אֶל־הָאֱלִילִם). Used after another noun it says that thing is of no worth; in the plural it is scripture's name for the gods of the nations, and Psa 96:5 sets it against אֱלֹהֵי “gods” in sound and against Yahweh in fact: they are nothings, he made the heavens.

senses.definition: After another noun, it says the thing is worth nothing: a healer who does not heal, a shepherd who does not shepherd, a vision with nothing in it.

evidence.note: “You are plasterers of a lie; you are all רֹפְאֵי אֱלִל, healers of nothing”: in parallel with שֶׁקֶר.
רֹעִי הָאֱלִיל, “the shepherd of nothing, who forsakes the flock.”
The prophets prophesy “a vision of a lie, and divination, and אֱלִיל, and the deceit of their heart”: listed with lie and deceit.

senses.gloss: the nothings: the gods of the nations, idols
senses.definition: In the plural, the gods the nations serve and the images made of them: things that are nothing, the work of men's hands, mute, and passing away before Yahweh.

evidence.note: “All the gods of the peoples are אֱלִילִים, but Yahweh made the heavens.”
The same words in David's psalm.
“Do not turn to the nothings, and do not make for yourselves molten gods.”
“Do not make for yourselves אֱלִילִם”, beside carved image and pillar.
The maker trusts in his work “to make mute nothings (אֱלִילִים אִלְּמִים)”.
“Their land is full of nothings; they bow to the work of their hands.”
“The nothings will pass away completely.”
Men throw their nothings of silver and gold to the moles and bats.
In parallel with עֲצַבִּים, images.
The nothings of Egypt tremble before Yahweh.
In parallel with גִּלּוּלִים.
“Ashamed are all who serve a carved image, who boast in nothings.”
“We know that an εἴδωλον is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God but one.”
What the nations sacrifice, they sacrifice to δαιμόνια and not to God.
δαιμόνια beside “idols of gold and silver …, which can neither see nor hear nor walk”.
“The Most High does not dwell in things made by hands.”
“Turn from these μάταια to the living God, who made heaven and earth.”

parallels.note: “Plasterers of a lie” beside “healers of nothing”; “a vision of a lie … and nothing”.
The carved image, served beside the nothings.
Images, in parallel with Samaria's nothings.
Idols, in parallel in Yahweh's word against Egypt.

opposites.note: “All the gods of the peoples are nothings, but Yahweh made the heavens.”

phrases.gloss: nothings of silver and nothings of gold

words.summary: A great tree, set beside the cedar for strength and height. Its tie to the negative is not known: Akkadian allānu and Ugaritic aln, “oak”, show a base ʾalān of its own, and scripture sets it beside the terebinth אֵלָה and אֵלוֹן (Isa 6:13; Hos 4:13), words of the entry for אַיִל.

senses.definition: A large, strong, long-lived tree of Bashan and the hills, used for timber and giving shade.

evidence.note: The Amorite was tall as the cedars and “strong as the oaks”.
“The oaks of Bashan” beside “the cedars of Lebanon, high and lifted up”.
Tyre's oars made of oaks of Bashan.
“Wail, oaks of Bashan.”
Sacrifice under oak, poplar and terebinth, “for its shade is good”.
Like terebinth and oak, whose stump remains when felled.
The idol maker takes a cypress or an oak from the forest.
Deborah is buried below Bethel under the oak, named אַלּוֹן בָּכוּת, “oak of weeping”.

words.summary: Once only, of the great tree at Shechem; whether it is the same tree as אַלּוֹן or the terebinth אֵלָה is not clear from the one verse.

senses.definition: The tree by Yahweh's holy place at Shechem, under which Joshua set up the stone of witness.

evidence.note: Joshua set up a great stone “under the אַלָּה that was by the holy place of Yahweh”.

cognates.note: Akkadian's negative of main clauses; with a different vowel, as Akkadian often has u where Hebrew has a.

The one cognate that could give the root a sense of its own, “be weak, be of no account”, from which both the negative and אֱלִיל “thing of no worth” could come. It shares the u of Akkadian ul. Rare (about fifteen attestations), and no dictionary consulted ties it to ul or to אֱלִיל, so it stays possible.

evidence.locator: armep x000074020, ulālu [weak] N “helpless person, weak”; armep x000145050, ulālu [weak (person)] N “weakling”; armep x000119560, ulālu [weak] AJ “helpless”

cognates.gloss: not, with the jussive and subjunctive (“do not”, “may … not”); also “verily”
cognates.note: Used as Hebrew אַל is, only with the jussive, never with a plain statement: al tṣr “do not besiege!”, al yšt “may he not put”.

evidence.locator: p. 179, §93 Glossary, al “not” with jussive (H. ʾal, Phoen. ʾl); al “verily”
p. 100, §65.22, dynamic negation al, used only with the jussive and the subjunctive (KTU 1.14:III:29; 2.41:22)

cognates.note: Both of Hebrew's uses: the prohibition, ʾl ʾl tptḥ ʿlty, “do not, do not open it” (Tabnit's coffin), and the bare refusal Al, “No!” (Plautus' Punic).

evidence.locator: pp. 50–51, ʾL V, part. NOT (negating the jussive); NO! (KAI 13.3–4; KAI 14.4–5; Poen. 1142)

cognates.note: With perfect and imperfect verbs and before nouns; “let them not hinder”; ʾl ʾs, “no one”.

evidence.locator: pp. 16–17, ʾL IV, negative particle: NOT, NO ONE (R 4088/4; R 4815/6)

cognates.gloss: not (negative prefix, as in ʾalbo “there is not”)

evidence.locator: p. 16, ʾL IV, sets Ethiopic ʾal-bo beside Sabaic ʾl and Hebrew ʾal

doctrine.statement: Scripture's name for the gods of the nations is אֱלִילִים, “nothings”, a word of the same letters as אַל “not”, and the verses say what it means: “all the gods of the peoples are nothings, but Yahweh made the heavens” (Psa 96:5; 1Ch 16:26); they are the work of men's hands (Isa 2:8), mute (Hab 2:18), and will pass away (Isa 2:18). Israel was told not to turn to them (Lev 19:4). Paul says the same in Greek: “an idol is nothing in the world, and there is no other God but one” (1Co 8:4); asked whether the idol or what is offered to it is anything, he answers that what the nations sacrifice they sacrifice “to δαιμόνια, and not to God” (1Co 10:19–20), and Revelation sets δαιμόνια beside idols of gold and silver “which can neither see nor hear nor walk” (Rev 9:20). The Greek psalm Paul's readers knew calls Psa 96:5's nothings δαιμόνια. So the δαιμόνια the nations served are the gods the Psalms call nothings, with no being or power of their own; the only living God is the one who made heaven and earth (Act 14:15).

Pro 12:28 sets “life” in the path of righteousness and, in parallel, אַל־מָוֶת, “no death”, on its way. Deathlessness is promised to a way of life, not said of man as he is: man is dust and returns to dust (Gen 3:19). Paul speaks the same way: God gives eternal life to those who “seek for glory and honour and immortality” by patient continuance in well doing (Rom 2:7), for “the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord” (Rom 6:23). So freedom from death is God's gift on the path of righteousness, not something every man already has.

note: Investigation of the root (2026-11-13). Hebrew אַל has no verb of its own in scripture. Taken under אלל because (1) scripture uses אַל itself as a noun “nothing” (Job 24:25, לְאַל) and (2) the noun אֱלִיל, “nothing, worthless”, has the same letters and is set beside it (Lev 19:4); Akkadian has both ul “not” and ulālu “weak, helpless”, which would give the root a sense, “be weak, be of no account”, but that is a possible cognate only. The other negatives (Ugaritic, Phoenician, Sabaic, Ge'ez, Akkadian ul) show the particle is old and common to the family, which says nothing either way about a root behind it. The evidence for the root is therefore weak to moderate, and the entry could equally be read as the particle keyed by its own consonants with אֱלִיל derived from it. Arabic has no ʾal negative (it uses لا), and the Peshitta's Syriac uses ܠܐ, not ʾal, so neither is cited. Aramaic outside scripture (Old and Imperial Aramaic ʾl “not”; Anderson–Moser ARM001358) is not cited: no Aramaic dictionary was read for it (CAL to consult). Ge'ez is cited from Anderson–Moser and Biella's remark only: Dillmann not read for አልቦ. The verb root אלל “be weak” is a BDB root with no verb in scripture (a.dp.aa, no tokens), and BDB's אֱלוּל (a.dp.ab) is only the written text of Jer 14:14 (read אֱלִיל), so neither is a word here. The oak words אַלּוֹן and אַלָּה (a.dq.ac, a.dq.ab), which the corpus files under אלל and the ayil entry left out, are kept here by spelling; their cognates (Akkadian allānu, Ugaritic aln) show a base ʾalān unrelated in meaning to the negative, and the terebinth אֵלָה and אֵלוֹן stand beside them (Isa 6:13; Hos 4:13): whether they belong with ayil (אול) is for review. The name Allon (a.dq.ad, 1Ch 4:37) and the place אַלּוֹן בָּכוּת are left out. Token counts: the corpus maps the surfaces אֶל and אַל to both a.dh.aa and a.di.aa, and every אַל also to the Aramaic xa.am.aa and to לֹא's l.ab.aa, so lexicon-support's counts are inflated: OSHB has about 730 אַל in the Hebrew and 4 in Daniel's Aramaic (Dan 2:24; 4:16; 5:10 twice). The preposition אֶל, which some have joined to אַל, is a word of the elah entry (a third-weak base, אֵלַי, אֱלֵי, as Arabic إِلَى), not of this one. The particle's senses are illustrated, not exhaustive.
